rules.rule: Regular intervals read as order or machinery, while steadily changing intervals read as movement, and irregular intervals feel organic.
rules.evidence: Regularevery gap the samereads as order, structure, machineryAcceleratingeach gap a quarter wider than the lastreads as movement, speed, recessionthe accentBrokenevery gap the same but one, which is doubledthe gap is the accent — nothing was added

rules.rule: A rhythm becomes a surface rather than a row of objects when repeated elements merge into one mass, losing individual inspection.
rules.evidence: Squint and ask whether the repeats have merged into one mass. If they have, they are a surface, not a row of objects.
